why: CC's clear of trouble cairn-tester-validation-store-py-persist-validation-... (2026-08-17) states '(c) run_proof persists through the door itself — NOT DONE; run_proof still takes a sink argument and the caller still chooses'. THAT IS FALSE and it now stands in a record of truth. Measured immediately after, at cairn/devices/tester/device.py:242-249: run_proof DOES persist through persist_validation, and it has since 2026-08-16 (ticket standing-gates-the-newest-link-and-run-proof-names-its-sink). The sink argument is REQUIRED and has no default, which is the same handoff closed in a different shape than the trouble's 2026-07-30 wording imagined — the caller cannot forget, because there is nothing to forget FROM. I read the word 'sink' in a grep, recognised it as a caller-chooses argument, and did not open the branch. Structure measured when behaviour was meant. THE CORRECTED RESIDUE, which is smaller than the clear says: of the three options the original trouble weighed, (b) is moot (the chain is gone) and (c) is DONE. Only (a) is genuinely outstanding, and only in part — the corpus census now exists as a build-time tooth inside test_validation_store.py (test_NO_SECOND_WRITER_EXISTS_IN_THE_CORPUS, green today at 105 files), but nothing fires it on its own, so detection remains incidental rather than designed. The one hole none of the layers closes is unchanged and was always known: a hand running as the same uid that writes bytes directly, covered only by the 0444 mode bit, the build-time census, and git. AND THE PHYSICS FINDING RIDING THIS ONE, which is why this is raised rather than edited: TroubleDevice.clear() appends to cleared_by and then refuses every later clear on the same ticket ('a second all-clear would overwrite the record of what actually fixed it'). That guard is right, and it means a clear containing a false statement can never be corrected through the lane's own door — the only routes are a hand-edit of the git-JSON (the defect the door exists to stop) or this: a NEW trouble that carries the correction and can never be found by anyone reading the original. Law 7 wants the error permanent in the record of truth, which it now is; what is missing is a way to make the record of truth carry its own correction. The shape the corpus already owns is validation_store's verdict_change/announce_verdict_change — a changed verdict announced before the replace lands — and the same shape would fit here: clear() growing an amend that appends a correction to cleared_by and announces it, rather than a second clear that overwrites.
